requirement:
A record's `references` digest MUST be rewritten only if the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` current reference set of its subject,
under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`, has the recorded digest.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.refactor.reference_digest` has one clause: a record's `references` digest "MUST be rewritten only if the mapped-back current reference set of its subject ... has the recorded digest". This is a behavioral guard on when a rewrite happens. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface that the implementation must use.

I considered whether the clause fixes how the guard is built. It does not. An implementation could recompute the mapped-back digest inline, in a helper, or in a different module. It could also compare it before or after other refactor steps. Each of these rewrites the digest in the same cases, so the clause is still met. The same holds for the cited `requirements.ci.reference_set` and the definition `requirements.refactor.mapped_back`. They define what the digest contains and how text is mapped back, and the clause only applies them as context. Their structural details, such as SHA-256 and sorted entries, belong to `requirements.ci.reference_set` and are judged there, not here.

No implementation roots were supplied. Since every clause here specifies only observable behavior, no implementation evidence is needed. Whether tests cover the guard is a separate question, left to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The requirement `requirements.refactor.reference_digest` has two behavioral obligations. First, a record's `references` digest is rewritten when the mapped-back current reference set of its subject has the recorded digest. Second, it is not rewritten when that set does not have the recorded digest. The first obligation implies the new digest is the one for the new reference set. I did not read the implementation. I judged only the supplied tests.

**Rewritten when the mapped-back set matches**
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` moves `fn[load]` to a new file.
  - Before the refactor, `errors(root)` reports `fn[load]` as stale.
  - After `--map src/config.rs#fn[load]=src/config/load.rs#fn[load]`, the record `rules.load` is listed as changed, and `errors(root)` is empty. That shows the digest was rewritten to the new reference set's digest.
  - The unrelated `rules.check` record is asserted byte-identical.
  - A second run reports `Changed 0 records`.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_file_rewrites_anchors_and_paths]` covers the other kind of mapped reference, a moved file with an `:impl:` anchor. After the refactor, `errors(root)` is empty and the whole snapshot matches the expected one apart from `rules.check`.

**Not rewritten when it does not match**
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_reference_set_changed_beyond_the_mapping_blocks_every_rewrite]` adds an `{impl}` that is not part of the move.
  - The report says the reference set of `core.load` changed.
  - The record bytes are asserted unchanged.
  - The report is asserted not to mention a text change, so the text and requirements-input rewrites are blocked as well.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_changed_reference_set_is_reported_on_a_record_reading_nothing_moved]` covers a record whose only recorded input is a glob. An extra `{impl}` is added alongside a moved node. The report names the reference-set change, and the record bytes are unchanged.

These scenarios cover the match case and the mismatch case, with function moves, file moves and a requirement rename in play. They also cover a record that has other rewrites pending and one that has none. The assertions check the digest outcome through the report, byte equality and validation. I found no gap.

text: :::{req} reference_digest
A record's `references` digest MUST be rewritten only if the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` current reference set of its subject,
under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`, has the recorded digest.
:::{req} reference_set

A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` edges, except a `{fixme}` inside a site of the definition under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: for each edge, its role and the file and
outline selector of the node the reference belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, or of the anchored file or
node, and, for a fenced reference in a source outside the book, the words of
its body under the word rule of {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
`{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
For a structural assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, the digest MUST additionally
include a versioned structural-assessment marker. A record predating structural
assessment MUST therefore be stale, including a legacy record with a wildcard
review version. Other assessments MUST retain their existing digest encoding.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{fixme}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, editing its commentary, or moving it to a different node
MUST therefore make the evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
:::{definition} mapped_back
:phrase: mapped-back
The *mapped-back* form of current text or a current address is the text or
address with each new side of the mappings replaced by its old side.
